newsitem.title: USA: Mid-States Q2 sales down 5.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mid-States Q2 sales down 5.7 pct.

text.p: Mid-States Plc said on Monday that its second-quarter sales were $31.3 million, or 19.2 million pounds sterling, down 5.7 percent in dollar terms and on a same location basis from the year-ago period.

For the year-to-date period, Mid-States said in a news release that its sales were $60.2 million, or 36.8 million pounds sterling, compared to $63.8 million, or 42 million pounds sterling, a year ago.
It gave no further details on earnings.
The company also said it will delist from the Nasdaq index to cut costs, as trading volumes have been insufficient to justify the expense of the listing.
Mid-States said it would revert to the British practice of reporting financial results half yearly rather than quarterly. Full results for the half-year were to be released in mid-September.
Mid-States on June 19 had said it expected sales and profits for the first six months to be significantly below the same period for 1996.
On Monday, however, the company said June sales were a little stronger than anticipated, and that the first two weeks of July were noticeably stronger than foreseen.
But the company added that it is too early to state whether there is any general improvement in the market.

Mid-States said its results continue to be affected by the weather, which was particularly wet during part of the second quarter, and also by increased competition in the marketplace, putting pressure on gross margins.
The company said it is responding with cost cuts, the benefits of which it expects to see reflected in its second-half results.
The company said it anticipates closing, selling or consolidating its underperforming operations, especially those outside its core markets in Tennessee, Kentucky and northern Alabama and Georgia.
Mid-States also said it plans to make management changes, including appointing a deputy chief executive.

The current chief executive, William Cook, said in the statement that he recently was diagnosed with cardiomyopathy, a disease affecting the heart muscle. Final tests in August will determine his status, Cook said.
The company distributes auto products in the southeastern United States.
